annotations.text:
Direction: refine what already exists.

The blue and green stay — parents recognise them. What changes is discipline. Each decision here is reversible on its own, so you can take five of six if one does not suit.

The whole proposal rests on one idea.

A PACE, a club, swimming, an e-learning module, a training course and an event ticket are not six features — they are six rows in one catalogue. A pupil gets one through an enrolment; every enrolment produces a billable line.

Get that spine right and the seventh offering, whatever it turns out to be, bills correctly without new billing code.

Read the eight decisions before costing any of this.

The first three are not matters of taste — getting price-snapshotting, integer money or the parent link wrong corrupts the fee ledger in ways that are slow and painful to unwind. The other five are policy only the school can settle.

The package builder is the only screen a human drives.

Everything after it — the statement, the portal unlock, the club register, the consent request — happens because of what was chosen here. So this is the one screen worth over-investing in.

Section A is the school fees proper. Section B is what was chosen for this pupil this term.

One document, one balance, two subtotals — so a parent can see the optional half of the bill and drop it next term without touching the core.

Same catalogue row, two delivery channels.

Swimming is delivered at school, so an enrolment puts the pupil on a register and raises a consent request. A coding module is delivered in the portal, so the same enrolment unlocks it. Neither needs its own billing path.

The ballot is the one thing here that must NOT reuse the spine.

Everything else is deliberately traceable — you need to know who owes what. A student council vote needs the opposite: two tables with no key between them, so nobody can see how a child voted.

The public site, rebuilt on the refined palette.

Home replaces the three broken testimonial photographs with initial monograms — no missing files, and nothing waiting on a photo shoot before launch.
Admissions now confirms DELIVERY, not just submission. Today a failed save to the school's own list is swallowed silently and the visitor still sees success.

The parent dashboard as it would look once a parent can actually be linked to their children.

Today this screen renders nothing at all — no child, no report, not even an explanation — because nothing in the live system ever sets that link. Billing makes that gap fatal rather than merely awkward.
Same story for supervisors: 'my students' and 'my classes' read zero today because accounts have no field connecting them to a staff record.
The Supervisors screen adds a 'portal login linked' badge — making visible the connection whose absence quietly empties a teacher's whole dashboard.

The report workflow is the best-built part of the system and needs no rework — only a term to exist, and clearer feedback when one does not. The five states now carry a fixed colour everywhere they appear.
Gallery gains real file upload — today staff must supply a path to an image already hosted elsewhere, which in practice means asking a developer.
Create Account gains the child picker. This one field is the difference between a working parent portal and an empty one — and now also between a parent seeing a bill and seeing nothing.
